why: Operator campground map posted on Nelson County's Stump Lake page (Stump_Lake_Park_Campground_Map-2013_Web.jpg, read 2026-11-12) numbers sites 1-131 in six sections. Only 'Cottonwood Corner Campsites (Temporary)' is marked for non-seasonal use: sites 77-79 and 94-100 (10) plus 3 primitive sites. That is 10 of 131 (7.6%), or 13 of 134 counting the primitive sites (9.7%), so under 10%. Park Rules (nelsonco.org Park Rules.docx, read 2026-11-12) put lessees on 'permanent camper sites' with sheds, decks and gazebos, and new lessees come off a waiting list. RV Life lists 10 sites; a 2015 RV Life reviewer: '95% are seasonal'.
name: Stump Lake Park Campground
inclusion_evidence: Nelson County Stump Lake Park & Village page (nelsonco.org, read 2026-11-12): reservation request form for Camper & RV Camping at $40/night and Primitive at $30/night. Rates page (business_detail_T10_R18): campsite with water and electricity $40/night or $240/week; tent/primitive $30/night or $180/week; cabin and pavilion apartment $100/night; contact campground manager 701-797-7234. ND HHS Statewide Licensed RV Parks/Campgrounds (07.17.2025) #271: NELSON COUNTY STUMP LAKE PARK CAMPGROUND, 63 Pavilion Rd, Pekin, owner NELSON COUNTY PARK BOARD, 130 lots. Google Maps 'Stump Lake Park': 4.6 stars on 36 reviews, 63 Pavilion Rd, phone 701-662-3928. RV Life 11390 'Stump Lake Campground': 1 star on 2 reviews, $$, 10 sites. Fifth wheels stayed in 2010 and 2015 (RV Life), so the 23-ft fit is not in doubt. No 'Stump Lake' entry in campgrounds.json; the nearest entries are 6050 Tolna City Park (2.9 km) and 6051 Tolna Dam (3.0 km), both separate places. gateways.py: none within 40 km. Public park, so no price gate applies.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-12, Esri World Imagery (frames of 1200, 900, 440, 320 and 260 m around 47.873-47.875, -98.343 to -98.354, all rendered). The park fills a wooded peninsula with Stump Lake on its W and S sides. The shoreline is a rocky riprap bank under a continuous tree belt, and most loops are packed with seasonal rigs; seasonal-only sites earn no value. On the operator map, the nightly ('Temporary') Cottonwood Corner sites lie on the east side by the entrance, away from the shore. Circle Drive, where a 2021 Campendium reviewer paid for one night, is an oval loop SE of the west ball field, about 30-40 m behind a wooded riprap bank. No named nightly pad sits within ~50 m of the water over open ground, so the value defaults down to not waterfront. A 'lakeview' could be argued for Circle Drive if AWH reverses the skip.

fees.note: Nelson County 2026: campsite with water and electricity $40/night, $240/week; tent/primitive $30/night, $180/week. Read 2026-11-12.

flags: BORDERLINE on test 4. The only count is the operator's 2013 map, still the map on the county's current page: 10 'Temporary' sites of 131 (7.6%), or 13 of 134 with the primitive sites (9.7%). Read as a skip under the AWH 2026-11-12 bands.

Evidence the nightly pool may be larger than the map's Temporary section: a 2021 Campendium reviewer paid $35 for one night in the 'Circle loop' (Circle Drive is sites 53-64 on the map, not in the Temporary section). If Circle Drive also sells nights, that would be about 22 of 131 (~17%): keep, with the 'more than half the sites are long-term residents' caveat. A 2023 Dyrt reviewer: 'Lots of regular campers who stay the season but also spots for visiting.'

Other long-stay tests. Test 2: nights are sold, via a county reservation-request form and the manager's phone, with no application. Test 3: no minimum is stated. Test 5: lessees' campers with sheds and decks are RV sites on leases, not homes for sale, so it passes.
Settling the count would take one phone call to the campground manager (701-797-7234): how many sites are kept for nightly campers. This agent made no calls.

Phones: the county page gives 701-797-7234 (Donna Rickford, campground manager). Google and The Dyrt still show 701-662-3928. The old stumplakepark.com says it is going down in 2027 and points to the county page.

If AWH keeps it: season roughly mid-May to Oct 12 (Park Board minutes 9-1-26: water shut off the weekend of Oct 12, docks out Oct 14). Hookups are water + electric (30 A per the 2021 review). Showers, flush restrooms, dump station, boat ramp, fish-cleaning station, cafe/bar. A note line would say 'Mostly seasonal: more than half the sites are long-term residents.'
